response: Yes, instrumental activities of daily living (IADLs) can predict dementia at 1- and 2-year follow-up. Research has shown that decline in IADLs, such as managing finances, cooking, and shopping, can be an early indicator of cognitive decline and a predictor of dementia. Individuals who experience difficulties with IADLs are more likely to develop dementia within a 1- to 2-year period.
